summary:
Orbit Vitals is a health monitoring app for astronauts, flight surgeons and mission control, built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. The farther a crew travels from Earth, the longer help takes: evacuation from the space station can take up to 36 hours, from the Moon 3 to 6 days, and from Mars it is not possible. Orbit Vitals helps notice health problems early, before they become emergencies.

The app compares every reading with that astronaut’s own normal, warning and critical limits, and alerts the flight surgeon when something is wrong. Only the flight surgeon can change a personal limit, always with a written note. Its rule-based decision support also checks real space station cabin data against NASA-STD-3001 and flags cases where an astronaut reports feeling unwell while all readings look normal. It does not diagnose; the flight surgeon decides.

It is a prototype: the astronauts are fictional, and their health readings are simulated and labelled. It is not a medical device.
details:
Orbit Vitals is a health-monitoring web app for crews far from Earth. It checks each astronaut's readings against that person's own limits across ten indicators: blood pressure, resting heart rate, SpO2, respiratory rate, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep, mood, body mass and radiation dose. A value is normal, a warning or critical depending on the limit set for that person.

Astronauts see an ID card, enter readings and report how they feel. The flight surgeon sees the crew sorted by severity, alerts, trend charts and a limit editor; every change to a limit records its reason. Default limits come from cited sources such as NEWS2 and NASA-STD-3001.

Medical decision support is rule-based and uses no language model. It flags cabin CO2, temperature, humidity and pressure outside NASA-STD-3001 limits, long runs in a warning band, and repeated reports of feeling unwell while readings look normal. Findings never change a status; the flight surgeon decides.

One profile uses real NASA OSDR EDA space station cabin data recorded in 2014. Other readings are simulated or entered by hand, and labelled as such.

Orbit Vitals is not a medical device and does not diagnose. The crew is fictional. Built with Python, FastAPI, MongoDB, React and TypeScript.
